title: SCTP: add a hint when SCTP association indexing is disabled (Fix for https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/17268)
description: SCTP: add a hint when SCTP association indexing is disabled

notes.body:
added 2 commits
  • 17960534 - 1 commit from branch wireshark:master
  • b6e5d16f - A fix for https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/17268:
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/2273/diffs?diff_id=152440757&start_sha=a179805177501578dce8773a992eb8db11dcfdb2)

As discussed in #17268, I'm not sure enabling it again by default is a good idea given the huge impact it can have.
Adding a hint taht it is disabled (like what we do for checksum computation) seems a very good idea.

I now added information about the disabled SCTP Association Indexing when decoding the sctp.assoc_index field.

Are use cases where SCTP Association Indexing causes performance impact really frequent? In the usual case, I assume the user just wants information about a certain SCTP assoc in a reasonably sized capture. The use case of processing huge PCAP traces where there is a real performance impact seems to be quite a corner case. It may be a more straightforward setting for the user to allow SCTP Association Indexing by default, and let the user disable it in the rare case where it really impacts performance.

I fixed the problem as a response to a user complaint. If i remember correctly the trace contsined a lot of failed sctp inits not unkommon in lab environments at least. It fealt bettet to have the default beahviour be robust and that users in the know can activate the funktion than the opposite. A better fix would be to fix the performance issue.

use expert_info ?

I'm neutral to the expert at info level (I tend to prefer the expert info but it's gonna be added to all the packets and thus in the expert information window).

The hint is not correct, the right way is not to tweak the advanced settings but activate the option in the SCTP preferences. IMHO is should only say association index: disabled
After more thoughts, an expert info will colorize all SCTP packets which does not seem to be a good idea.
The user should also get a hint where to change the setting. Otherwise, the user's immediate question is: "But how can I enable this?"

We do not add any hint for all other protocols (like checksum validation in TCP/UDP/...) and as far as I know people are able to find it. The SCTP preference are even accessible from the right click menu in the packet that is much fater than going from the top level bar.
